headline: CoStar's growth accelerates as Domain lifts residential
summary_short: CoStar's Q2 2026 revenue rose 18% y/y to $925M as Residential Real Estate (+33% y/y, boosted by the Domain acquisition) outgrew Commercial Real Estate (+8% y/y), while gross margin held near 79% and diluted EPS improved to $0.14 from $0.01 a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue grew 18% y/y to $925M, led by Residential Real Estate (+33% to $444M, including $70M from Domain) and Commercial Real Estate (+8% to $481M on CoStar subscriber growth and price increases). Gross margin expanded to 79% from 78%. Net income rose to $55M from $6M on revenue growth and a lower tax rate (26% vs 73%), tied to prior-year U.K. losses under a full valuation allowance. Cash fell to $1,266M from $3,629M a year ago on the Domain/Matterport acquisitions and $589M of first-half buybacks; CoStar separately agreed in May 2026 to acquire Zonda for ~$800M cash, closing H2 2026. No numeric guidance was given beyond commentary that Commercial growth should moderate and Residential growth accelerate in 2026.

drivers.explanation: Residential Real Estate +$109M (33%) on the Domain acquisition ($70M) and higher memberships/properties advertised, partly offset by lower average price; Commercial Real Estate +$35M (8%) on CoStar subscriber growth, inflation-based price increases, and STR Benchmarking sales.

Gross margin rose to 79% from 78% as revenue growth outpaced a 17% rise in cost of revenue, which included higher amortization from the Matterport and Domain acquisitions and Domain-related web hosting, data, and personnel costs.

Revenue growth flowed through against a Q1 base with only $76M of opex growth (G&A fell 7% on a Brown Judgment recovery gain), so operating leverage improved sharply off a near-zero prior-quarter base.
Driven by higher net income and a lower diluted share count (404.4M vs 424.3M y/y) from the new $1.5B buyback program, including a $500M accelerated share repurchase completed in March 2026.
Reflects the revenue and margin gains above plus a lower effective tax rate of 26% (vs 73% a year ago), which the company attributes to prior-year U.K. losses subject to a full valuation allowance.
Cash fell from $3,629M to $1,266M y/y mainly on the Domain and Matterport acquisitions completed in 2025 and $589M of first-half 2026 share repurchases under the Stock Repurchase Program.
Not explained in the release beyond the general effect of share repurchases reducing equity through treasury stock.

Growth accelerated on the Domain acquisition; the company expects Commercial Real Estate growth to moderate and Residential Real Estate growth to accelerate for full-year 2026, and agreed in May 2026 to acquire Zonda for ~$800M cash.
